author: Jordan B Peterson
description: Why would a man who freed an entire nation from slavery be forbidden from entering the land he spent his life trying to reach? In this lecture, Jordan Peterson traces the extraordinary story of Moses, from a violent act that drives him into exile, through a mysterious encounter with a burning bush, to a confrontation with Pharaoh and forty years of wandering in the desert. Along the way, an ancient story about escaping tyranny becomes something far more personal: an examination of why freedom can be terrifying, why people cling to the very things that oppress them, and how even the most well-intentioned leaders can become the thing they set out to destroy. But the most unsettling revelation comes at the very end of Moses' journey, when a single act costs him everything he has worked toward. What the story of Exodus reveals about leadership isn't just a lesson for kings and nations. It's a question about the responsibility each of us is willing to bear, and what happens when we refuse.
title: Why You Should Have Hope Even When the Future Looks Terrifying
